chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Look at your heart, for if it rejects your companion, then know that one of you has done something wrong.
ai.seo_question: How to know if a friendship is spiritually healthy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the heart as a spiritual barometer for the state of one's relationships, suggesting that sudden discomfort signals a deviation in character. This introspective advice aligns with the Shia emphasis on *mu'asharah* (companionship) and the concept of *fitrah*, where the innate nature detects spiritual dissonance. It serves as a practical guide for believers to assess whether the change lies within themselves or their companion, fostering self-correction or mindful separation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Zanar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Look at your heart, for if it rejects your companion, then know that one of you has done something wrong’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mada’ini from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
See your heart. If it dislikes your friend then notice that one of you have done something newly wrong.’”
